🇲🇽📊 <u>Hacienda: Mexico's Economy Is Picking Up Speed</u>

Speaking at the Milken Institute's Global Investors Symposium, Finance Secretary Édgar Amador said the economy is "gaining momentum" after a weak first half. INEGI's monthly activity index grew 3.4% in July and 3.5% in August, year on year. Amador gave four reasons: a young, increasingly skilled workforce with rising wages and falling labor poverty; investment recovering, both public and private; a dynamic export sector; and inflation converging to Banxico's target.

He added that companies are reinvesting their profits, a sign "that the companies already operating in Mexico are choosing to expand their activities in the country." (El Economista)

🇲🇽🇵🇸 <u>Israeli Soldiers in Chiapas Schools</u>

In June, parents in the Tsotsil community of Zinacantán, Chiapas, reported men who identified themselves as Israel Defense Forces combatants, there through a group called Heroes for Life, doing painting and maintenance at the Narciso Mendoza primary school. Community members demanded to know who had authorized the visit.

It wasn't a one-off. On January 10, Chiapas's state security secretary Óscar Aparicio met Israel's police attaché for Latin America, Yaron Elyashiv, to discuss "security, intelligence and crime prevention" cooperation. In May he met Israel's consul to strengthen "strategic alliances." President Sheinbaum has been clear that the federal government has no military relationship with Israel.

🇲🇽🚰 <u>Guadalajara Water Plan: 24.7 Billion Pesos, No Debt, No Privatization</u>

Sheinbaum and Jalisco governor Pablo Lemus announced a joint water plan for metropolitan Guadalajara: about 14.5 billion pesos from the federal government and 10.2 billion from the state. Conagua will build two aqueducts, a 42 km line carrying 8,000 liters per second to Cerro del Cuatro and a second line from the Calderón dam to San Gaspar. Both start in early 2027.

Federal money means Jalisco no longer has to take on the debt it had planned. Jalisco has also taken back Toluquilla plant #4, privatized in 2012 and delivering only 10% of its promised capacity. In Lemus's words: "No debt, no privatization and no increase in water rates."

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>Mexico Opens the UN Debate Against the Cuba Blockade</u>

Mexico's ambassador Héctor Vasconcelos opened Wednesday's General Assembly debate on the US blockade of Cuba, calling it contrary to international law and "a structural obstacle" to the island's development. "No people should be forced to face these conditions as a result of unilateral coercive measures," he said, and he asked Washington to take Cuba off its list of state sponsors of terrorism.

The resolution passed for the 34th time: 130 in favor, 17 against, 25 abstentions. Colombia, Ecuador and Costa Rica joined the US and Israel in voting no. Mexico's position hasn't moved in more than six decades.

🇲🇽📊 <u>Senate Passes Mexico's 2027 Revenue Law: 10.6 Trillion Pesos</u>

Mexico's Senate approved the 2027 Revenue Law 79–34, unchanged from the Chamber of Deputies' version. It projects 10.636 trillion pesos in total revenue, about 6.26 trillion of it from taxes, mainly ISR and IVA. Morena, PVEM and PT voted for it, and PAN, PRI and MC voted against. Only the income-tax (ISR) changes go back to the Chamber.

🇲🇽🇫🇷 <u>Le Pen Launches Her Campaign Against "Mexicanization"</u>

Marine Le Pen opened her presidential campaign by turning Mexico into a bogeyman. In front of about 8,500 supporters she promised to stop the "Mexicanization" of France: "We will eradicate these criminal organizations without mercy, treating them as terrorists." It's the same script Washington uses, with Mexico as the cautionary tale, the "terrorist" label as the tool, and borders and migration as the real agenda.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>FGR: An Inmate's TV Interview Is Not Evidence</u>

Former vice admiral Manuel Roberto Farías Laguna, held in the Altiplano prison over the huachicol fiscal fuel-smuggling network, answered a TV network's questionnaire, called himself a "scapegoat" and named names. Mexico's Attorney General's Office (FGR) replied that 17 people have already been arrested and prosecuted over the Challenge Procyon tanker, and that his claims are "hearsay testimony." If he has evidence, he can bring it to a judge, not to the media.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum: Audit the INE All the Way Back to Córdova</u>

President Sheinbaum wants the Federal Audit Office (ASF) to audit the INE thoroughly, under Taddei and under Lorenzo Córdova before her. The same suppliers, Cajas Graf, Formas Finas, Corporativo Zeg and Comercializadora JVLY, got contracts in both eras. AMLO's Financial Intelligence Unit froze their accounts, and the companies kept operating thanks to a court injunction. "There can be no shadow of conflict of interest or corruption. It has to be opened up, made transparent, and it cannot happen again."

🇲🇽🇺🇸 <u>Ebrard: Nobody Buys More From the US Than Mexico</u>

Americans keep telling Marcelo Ebrard that Mexico should be grateful for how much it sells them. His answer: yes, and so should they. Mexico buys about 350 billion dollars a year from the United States, more than China, Germany and Japan combined. And US buyers pick Mexican goods for price, quality and reliability, because "we don't steal anyone's technology."

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Three Taddei Appointees Out as Blanca Cruz Takes Over the INE</u>

Mexico's electoral institute has a new interim president. Councillor Blanca Cruz García took the INE's top seat after Guadalupe Taddei's resignation, and the first thing she announced was a review of every senior official. Three resigned on day one, among them Mario Alfonso Burciaga Esparza, head of Material Resources, the office that handles the contracts now under audit. Cruz promised to restore collegial decision-making and to make it easy for investigators to do their job.
banner: INE: INTERIM CHIEF, 3 TADDEI AIDES OUT
